structured.reason: The description stays positive. It contains no explicit weaknesses, no hedges or concessions such as "although," "despite," or "may require," and no backhanded replies to the reviews. The reviews raise complaints (the glue did nothing, lashes became brittle and fell out), but the description never mentions or alludes to them. Its claims are plain positives: "can last up to a month," "minimal effort," "gentle touch," "salon-inspired results." The opening "Tired of straight lashes that won't hold a curl?" is problem/solution framing about the buyer, which is allowed. The skin-test line ("If you notice no discomfort or irritation, you can proceed") is a routine care instruction that does not suggest fragility, so it does not count as a conditional caveat. The "Safe Application, Every Time" heading is a positive claim with no concession attached, so it does not count as a defensive reaction to the lash-loss complaints.
